sections.h2: Who sends the Manatee County tax bill?
sections.html:
Manatee County splits the job between two offices. The property appraiser sets value, and the tax collector mails and collects the bill. Each year the appraiser mails the TRIM notice, the collector mails the bill, and the money moves on to the local taxing authorities.

Questions about an exemption, a parcel record or an assessed value go to the Manatee County Property Appraiser. Questions about what is owed, which discount applies or whether a certificate has been issued go to the Manatee County Tax Collector. Recorded deeds and liens sit with the clerk of court at manateeclerk.com.

  • Property appraiser: parcel search, homestead e-filing, tangible personal property returns, TRIM notices, value reviews and Value Adjustment Board information.
  • Tax collector: bills, payments, installment plans, delinquent accounts and the annual tax certificate sale.
  • Clerk: recorded deeds, mortgages and liens, plus tax deed sales run for the county.

Bills go out in early November, and the discount shrinks month by month until the gross amount comes due March 31. The 2026 roll opened for collection with a November 2 mailing.

A deadline is met in one of three ways: in person by 5:00 p.m., by postmark, or online by 11:59 p.m. The discount schedule for 2026 bills is below.

Discount periods for paying 2026 Manatee County bills in full
Payment windowDiscount
November 2 to December 34%
December 4 to December 313%
January 1 to January 312%
February 1 to February 281%
March 1 to March 31No discount, last day before delinquency

sections.h2: Can Manatee County owners pay in installments?
sections.html:
Yes. Section 197.222 of the Florida Statutes lets the tax collector offer four quarterly payments, and the prior year's taxes must have exceeded $100 to join. The application deadline is May 1 of the assessment year.

The Manatee installment ladder:

  • June 30, first installment: 6% discount. Paid by July 31, it earns no discount.
  • September 30, second installment: 4.5% discount.
  • December 31, third installment: 3% discount.
  • March 31, fourth installment: no discount, and the last day before delinquency.

If you sell partway through a plan year, tell the collector. The closing payoff has to cover whatever remains.

sections.h2: Email reminders from the tax collector
sections.html:
The collector sends free property tax email alerts when taxes are due, when a payment posts, when a discount period is about to end and when taxes go delinquent. A tutorial on its site explains signup, and a separate management page lets you change or delete alerts.

Sellers can put this to use during a listing. An alert on the parcel you are selling confirms that a payment posted before the closing agent orders a payoff. The collector's help center also has checklists and answers for an office visit, and appointments are listed on its website.

With an escrowed loan, confirm with the servicer who is paying, since a lender payment and an owner payment can overlap.

sections.h2: What happens if Manatee County taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
Anything still owed after March 31 is delinquent on April 1 and can pick up fees, interest and collection costs. From then on the collector counts a payment only when it is received by the last business day of the month, and a postmark does not count.

Certificates are sold on all unpaid items by June 1. Manatee runs one annual sale and issues a certificate on any parcel still unpaid, and paying the taxes cancels it. Certificates nobody buys go to the county, and investors can buy them later from the county-held list.

A certificate is not a deed. Under section 197.502, a holder who waits two years can ask for a tax deed, and the collector then lists the owner, lienholders and any contract-for-deed buyer for notice. On a homestead property the opening bid is higher, because one-half of the latest assessed value is added.

sections.h2: Exemptions that lower a Manatee County bill
sections.html:
Apply at the property appraiser, whose website offers electronic filing for homestead. The paper form is DR-501, and the first state deadline is in early March.

  • Homestead takes up to $50,000 off taxable value. Only the first $25,000 reduces school taxes.
  • Once a home is homesteaded, a state cap limits how fast its assessed value can climb. The state chart shows 2.7% for 2026.
  • Investment and second-home parcels face a different ceiling of 10 percent a year.
  • Portability lets a long-time homesteader move the cap benefit to a new home, using Form DR-501T.
  • Homestead tax deferral goes through the tax collector, on Form DR-570, for owners who qualify.

Renting the home out or moving away ends homestead. The appraiser also takes reports of suspected exemption fraud through a confidential form.

Start with the August TRIM notice. The appraiser's homepage invites owners who think a value is wrong to ask for a review of their property data and assessed value, and it links the Value Adjustment Board page for those who want a formal hearing.

A formal petition has to be filed through the clerk within 25 days of the notice date, using one of the DR-486 forms. A denied exemption has its own 30-day clock. Both run from mailing dates printed on the paper you receive, so read it the day it arrives.

Business owners with tangible personal property report to the appraiser each year by April 1 and can request a 30-day extension from the same office.

sections.h2: The tax bill at a sale
sections.html:
An open bill rarely stops a sale. The closing agent can settle it from the buyer's funds, and the title company can order the payoff. The collector confirms the account standing and whether any certificate exists. Treat a certificate as a title problem to settle early.

The state deed stamp rate is 70 cents for each $100 of price, collected by the clerk as the deed is recorded. A cash sale shortens the timeline because no lender appraisal or underwriting has to finish first, and it leaves the tax items just as they were.

If the parcel already has back taxes or a deed application, get the figure from the collector in writing before the closing date is set.

  1. Ask the collector for the account standing.
  2. Give the closing agent any installment history.
  3. Check the settlement statement's tax line against the collector's number.

sections.h2: Will the next owner pay the same tax?
sections.html:
Probably not. Your capped assessment ends with the sale, and the parcel moves to full market-based value the next January. A buyer who budgets from the old bill can be surprised.

The appraiser's site posts the preliminary roll, reports and earlier years' millage for anyone who wants to compare. For the rate on one address, ask the collector or appraiser, since each taxing authority sets its own.

faqs.q: Who answers questions about a Manatee County tax bill?
faqs.a: The tax collector covers bills, payments, installments and delinquent accounts. The property appraiser covers values and exemptions, and the clerk covers recorded deeds and liens.

faqs.q: Does Manatee County reward early payment?
faqs.a: Yes. For 2026 bills the discount is 4% from November 2 to December 3, 3% from December 4 to December 31, 2% in January and 1% in February. March has none.

faqs.q: When do Manatee County taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: April 1. Unpaid parcels then enter the collector's yearly certificate sale, and paying the taxes cancels a certificate.

faqs.q: Can a Manatee County owner list a house while tax is unpaid?
faqs.a: Yes. Closing can absorb what is owed. The title company orders the payoff, and the collector confirms whether a certificate exists.

faqs.q: When must I apply for a homestead exemption in Manatee County?
faqs.a: File with the property appraiser by March 1. The home must be your permanent residence on January 1, and electronic filing is available.
